messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 — elevated 5xx rate detected in heartland region (us-mid). Alerting on-call.

sara (oncall): seeing the page. investigating now. rough ETA 15m. @mike can you join for infra-side triage?

mike (sre): on it. quick check: gateway 5xx spike from us-mid edge -> 60s window shows 12% error rate, latency up ~300ms. sending first triage.

ingrid (eng-runtime): logs from runtime show a sharp increase in KV cache misses followed by repeated upstream 502 from model-proxy pool: "upstream read timeout". sample:
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] proxy: GET /v1/generate -> 502 upstream read timeout (node=mlworker-7)
[2026-03-15T14:03:22Z] runtime: kvcache miss key=conv_abc123 latency=12ms
```

mike (sre): stack-level check: mlworker pool healthy overall but three nodes in us-mid showing OOM-kill restarts in last 6m. could be noisy GC or memory leak.

rahul (eng-infra): oncall metrics confirm container restarts ~3, memory usage trending to 98% on mlworker-7/8/9. investigating recent deploys — nothing in last 2h. network flaps looked normal.

sara (oncall): impact: 12% of requests from us-mid seeing 5xx. customers with strict latency SLAs likely affected. @liz can support craft a lite comms if we need to notify customers?

liz (support): yep — standby. need final impact numbers and expected recovery time before sending. will prep templates.

ingrid (eng-runtime): hot mitigation idea: shift traffic away from us-mid to us-east for models that are failing. we have routing weights toggle in console. if we steer 50% to us-east it should reduce error rate quickly. also consider evicting cached large KV entries on bad nodes to free memory.

mike (sre): agree. plan — (1) immediately reduce traffic to us-mid by 60% to us-east (via route weight), (2) cordon + drain problematic mlworker nodes, (3) scale up mlworker pool by +2 nodes pre-warmed in us-mid, (4) enable per-route fallback to quantized model variant if CPU/memory pressure persists.

rahul (eng-infra): implementing step 1 now: toggling route weights. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set-weight --region us-mid --dest us-east --weight 0.6 --route model/gpt-small
```

ops-bot: routing change accepted, new weights will propagate in ~20s.

mike (sre): step 2: cordon/drain targeted nodes (mlworker-7/8/9). running:
```
kubectl cordon mlworker-7 && kubectl drain mlworker-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

ingrid (eng-runtime): while draining, I'm issuing a KV eviction on those nodes for large conversation caches to free memory:
```
runtime-cli evict-cache --node mlworker-7 --pattern conv_* --size-gt 1MB
```

sara (oncall): monitoring metrics now. tell me when routing change fully propagated.

ops-bot: routing weights propagated: us-mid->us-east 60% reroute in effect.

mike (sre): immediate drop in 5xx from 12% -> 3% within 45s. latency trending down. continuing drain/scale.

rahul (eng-infra): added +2 mlworker instances in us-mid (pre-warmed). new node IDs mlworker-21, mlworker-22. autoscaler adjusted.

ingrid (eng-runtime): patched runtime to prefer local cache on healthy nodes; fallback to quantized model enabled for the heaviest routes. monitoring for regressions.

sara (oncall): customer impact: affected % down to ~2.5% of requests in us-mid. low-risk customers unaffected. @liz can proceed with a brief message saying partial degradation mitigated, we're continuing remediation.

liz (support): drafting: "We observed elevated error rates in our Heartland (us-mid) region earlier. Traffic was partially rerouted to other regions and the issue is being mitigated — a small portion of requests may have been affected. We'll follow up once fully resolved." Will hold until final confirmation.

mike (sre): follow-ups: (a) collect OOM logs from mlworker-7/8/9 and core-dump if present, (b) run heap profile on new nodes, (c) add temporary circuit-breaker to limit in-flight requests per node to avoid repeat saturation.

ingrid (eng-runtime): capturing heap profiles and core logs now. adding temporary circuit-breaker config:
```
runtime-config set circuit_breaker --max_inflight 80 --region us-mid --ttl 10m
```

ops-bot: circuit-breaker applied.

sara (oncall): leaving this thread to @mike/@ingrid for remediation. I'll stay on standby for escalation. current status: degraded -> partial mitigation in place, customer impact reduced. next update in 30m or on major change.

customer-success: can you tag impacted customer list? we want to proactively reach out to top 5 affected customers.

mike (sre): will attach query later. initial list is being generated.

ingrid (eng-runtime): timeline note for postmortem: immediate symptom = memory churn + upstream read timeouts; likely working set > cache capacity on mlworker nodes leading to OOMs. root cause TBD (could be workload spike + bad eviction heuristics).

sara (oncall): closing page for now — moving to monitoring state. create postmortem ticket and add me and mike as responders. thanks everyone for the quick rally :thumbsup:

incident-bot: page resolved (SEV2 -> MONITORING) at 2026-03-15T14:17:56Z.
